paragraphs: Rabbi Chiyya, his son, [described here as] Rabbi Perida’s grandfather; Sanhedrin 82a.

notes.text: The Hebrew describes Rabbi Chiyya as Avuya’s son and Rabbi Perida’s grandfather. Sanhedrin82a explicitly names Chiyya bar Avuya but leaves the grandfather in the adjoining skull narrative unnamed; that relationship has not been independently established here.

The saved named Davidson Sanhedrin 82a paragraph names Chiyya bar Avuya as reporter of the skull inscription and then calls the finder only “Rabbi Perida’s grandfather.” Identifying reporter and finder is Hyman’s reading of their juxtaposition, not an explicit genealogy in that paragraph. The existing qualified English and source hold are retained.

The text of Sanhedrin 82a calls the finder “Rabbi Perida’s grandfather.” Rashi on that passage explicitly identifies him as Rabbi Chiyya bar Avuya. Hyman likewise gives that identification in his entry on Rabbi Perida (vol. III, p. 1032). The earlier note records the narrower reading of the Gemara and the earlier stage of review.
